tool.name: RiboHub: Generate GWIPS Track Hub
tool.description: Build a GWIPS-viz compatible RiboSeq track hub from bigWig and bigBed files
tool.command:
#import uuid #set $rand_id = str(uuid.uuid4())[:15] chmod 777 /export/galaxy/hub_output 2>/dev/null || true; mkdir -p /export/galaxy/hub_output/genomebrowsertrack/${rand_id} &&
## If user typed SRR IDs directly, write them to a temp file #if str($sample_source.source_type) == "typed" #if $sample_source.srr_text.strip() echo '${sample_source.srr_text}' | tr ',' '\n' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' > '$__new_file_path__/srr_list.txt' && #end if #end if
/tool_deps/_conda/bin/ribohub generate
## Sample input #if str($sample_source.source_type) == "file" and $sample_source.samples --samples '$sample_source.samples' #elif str($sample_source.source_type) == "typed" and $sample_source.srr_text.strip() --samples '$__new_file_path__/srr_list.txt' #end if
--output-dir /export/galaxy/hub_output/genomebrowsertrack/${rand_id} --output-format 'single-file' --genome '$genome'
## Track selection #set $kind_list = [] #if $tracks.kinds.kind_all #silent $kind_list.append("all") #end if #if $tracks.kinds.kind_unique #silent $kind_list.append("unique") #end if #if $tracks.kinds.kind_multi #silent $kind_list.append("multi") #end if #if $kind_list --kinds '${",".join($kind_list)}' #end if
#if $tracks.with_aggregates --with-aggregates #else --no-aggregates #end if
#if $tracks.with_regions --with-regions #else --no-regions #end if
## Metadata filter #if $metadata_filter --filter '$metadata_filter' #end if
## Hub identity #if $options.hub_name --hub-name '$options.hub_name' #end if
--metadata '/data/metadata.csv' --data-dir /data/bigwig --base-url http://localhost/data $options.dry_run
## Copy output to Galaxy history #if not $options.dry_run #set $hub_name_val = $options.hub_name if $options.hub_name else "RiboSeqHub" && echo "http://localhost/genomebrowsertrack/${rand_id}/${hub_name_val}.hub.txt" > '$hub_output' #end if

param.name: source_type
param.label: How do you want to provide sample IDs?
param.option: Use metadata filter only (no sample list)

param.name: samples
param.label: Sample list
param.help: CSV with SRR IDs in the first column or plain text with one SRR per line.

param.name: srr_text
param.label: SRR accessions
param.help: Paste one or more SRR accessions, separated by commas, spaces or newlines. Example: SRR9295900, SRR9295905, SRR9295906, SRR9295907, SRR9295908

param.name: genome
param.label: Genome assembly
param.help: Reference genome the bigWig files were aligned to.

param.name: metadata_filter
param.label: Filter samples by metadata (optional)
param.help:
Narrow your sample set using metadata column values. Works on its own or combined with a sample list.
Format: COLUMN=value or COLUMN=val1/val2 (OR within one field). Comma-separate for AND across fields.
Available columns and example values: • LIBRARYTYPE = Ribo-Seq, RNA-Seq, CLIP, QTI-Seq, RiboTag • TISSUE = Bone, Ovary, Testis, Blastula, Gastrula • CELL_LINE = HEK293, U2OS, HeLa, A549, Neuroblast • CONDITION = Control, Mutant, KO, KD, Wild Type, Test • INHIBITOR = Cycloheximide, Harringtonine, Lactimidomycin, Frozen • REPLICATE = 1, 2, 3
Examples: CELL_LINE=HEK293 → all HEK293 samples CONDITION=Control/TEST → stress OR starvation CELL_LINE=HEK293,CONDITION=Control → HEK293 AND control INHIBITOR=Cyloheximide/Harringtonine → cycloheximide OR harringtonine treated

param.name: with_aggregates
param.label: Include strand overlays
param.help: Overlays forward and reverse strand signal in a single track per sample using a transparent multiWig view. Useful for quickly spotting strand-specific translation activity without switching between tracks.

param.name: with_regions
param.label: Include region annotations (bigBed)
param.help: Displays ORF annotation tracks (bigBed) alongside the signal if available for the sample. Shows translated regions, uORFs and other features detected by the RiboSeqOrg pipeline.

param.name: kind_all
param.label: All reads
param.help: Combined unique + multimapped signal. This is the default and usually what you want for an overview.

param.name: kind_unique
param.label: Unique reads only
param.help: Uniquely mapped reads. Higher confidence per-position but may underrepresent repetitive regions.

param.name: kind_multi
param.label: Multimapped reads only
param.help: Reads mapping to multiple genomic locations. Useful for examining signal at paralogs, pseudogenes and repeat elements.

param.name: hub_name
param.label: Hub name
param.help: Custom identifier for the generated hub (default: RiboSeqHub). Used as the filename and the label shown in the GWIPS-viz hub list. No spaces allowed.

param.name: dry_run
param.label: Dry run (preview only)
param.help: Shows how many samples were found, which bigWig files matched and what the hub would contain, without writing any files. Run this first when working with large sample sets to check your filter before committing to a full build.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What is RiboHub?**
RiboHub generates UCSC Genome Browser track hubs from ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) bigWig files produced by the RiboSeqOrg pipeline. The resulting hub can be loaded directly into **GWIPS-viz** or the standard UCSC browser to visualise translation data in genomic context.
------
**Quick start**
1. Choose how to provide samples: type SRR accessions directly, upload a file, or let the metadata filter select them for you. 2. Pick the genome assembly your data was aligned to. 3. Click **Execute**. The output is a URL, paste it into GWIPS-viz under *My Hubs → paste URL* to load the hub.
------
**Providing samples**
You have three options:
- **Type SRR accessions**: paste accessions like ``SRR9295900, SRR9295905`` directly into the text box. Commas, spaces and newlines all work as separators. - **Upload a file**: a CSV (SRR IDs in the first column) or plain text (one SRR per line). - **Metadata filter only**: skip the sample list entirely and let the filter select samples based on their metadata properties.
You can combine a sample list with a metadata filter to narrow further: only samples appearing in *both* the list and the filter will be included.
------
**Track types explained**
*Strand overlays* Forward and reverse strand signal rendered as a transparent overlay in a single track per sample (multiWig). The default Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe palette uses orange for forward and blue for reverse. This is the fastest way to spot strand-specific translation.
*Region annotations (bigBed)* ORF annotations from the RiboSeqOrg pipeline displayed as coloured blocks beneath the signal tracks. Includes annotated CDS, upstream ORFs (uORFs), downstream ORFs and novel translation events.
*Read types* - **All** = combined unique + multimapped signal (start here). - **Unique** = uniquely mapped only (higher confidence per position). - **Multi** = multimapped only (useful for repetitive regions and paralogs).
------
**Metadata filter**
The metadata filter lets you select samples by their biological properties without needing to look up individual SRR accessions. The filter operates on the RiboSeqOrg metadata CSV hosted on the server.
*Syntax*
::
COLUMN=value single value COLUMN=value1/value2 OR within one column COL1=val,COL2=val AND across columns
*Available columns*
================ ===================================================== Column Example values ================ ===================================================== LIBRARYTYPE Ribo-Seq, RNA-Seq, CLIP, QTI-Seq, RiboTag TISSUE Bone, Ovary, Testis, Blastula, Gastrula CELL_LINE HEK293, U2OS, HeLa, A549, Neuroblast CONDITION Control, Mutant, KO, KD, Wild Type, Test INHIBITOR Cycloheximide, Harringtonine, Lactimidomycin, Frozen REPLICATE 1, 2, 3 ================ =====================================================
*Examples*
::
CELL_LINE=HEK293 → all HEK293 samples regardless of condition
CONDITION=High/Test → samples Test OR High
CELL_LINE=HEK293,CONDITION=Control → HEK293 control samples only
INHIBITOR=Cycloheximide/Harringtonine,TISSUE=Bone → bone samples treated with cycloheximide or harringtonine
------
**Dry run**
Enable *Dry run* under Hub options to preview sample counts, matched bigWig files and hub structure without generating anything. Recommended before building hubs from broad metadata filters that may match hundreds of samples.
------
**Tips**
- Hub names cannot contain spaces. Use underscores or hyphens instead (e.g. ``HEK293_CHX_timecourse``). - If no samples match your filter, the tool will report zero matches and exit cleanly. Check column names and values for typos. - All columns and values are **case-sensitive**: use ``HEK293`` not ``hek293``. - The strand overlay is the most useful single view for quick inspection. Start there and drill into individual read types if needed.
